relation_proposals.evidence_context: Foundation LLMs recognize patterns so well that foundation LLMs often need only a modest amount of additional training to perform a specific task. This additional training is called fine-tuning. Fine-tuning trains a foundation LLM on examples that are specific to the task of the application. Engineers can often fine-tune a foundation LLM with only a few hundred to a few thousand training examples. Standard fine-tuning is computationally expensive, because standard fine-tuning updates the weights and biases of every parameter on each backpropagation iteration. Parameter-efficient tuning is a less expensive alternative to standard fine-tuning, because parameter-efficient tuning updates only a subset of the parameters on each backpropagation iteration. A fine-tuned LLM usually makes better predictions on its task than the foundation LLM does. A fine-tuned LLM has the same number of parameters as the foundation LLM it came from. For example, fine-tuning a foundation LLM that has ten billion parameters produces a fine-tuned LLM that also has ten billion parameters.
